insights.title: The dataset-wide observation mean is 11.95 per 100,000.
insights.detail: The mean across 2,843 observed country-year records is 11.95; the median is 10.64.
insights.caveat: This weights each reported record equally, not each country equally, and coverage varies by year.

insights.title: The highest simple yearly mean is in 1982 (14.76).
insights.detail: There are 52 entities reporting in the peak year.
insights.caveat: The number and composition of reporting entities change over time; the fixed eight-entity panel peaks in 1998 (12.21).

insights.title: Lithuania has the highest eligible country mean (35.13).
insights.detail: The ranking requires at least 10 observations; Lithuania has 23.
insights.caveat: Without that rule, the raw top three are Lithuania (35.1; n=23), Guyana (30.8; n=3), Russia (30.8; n=24); short series such as Guyana (3) are less comparable.

insights.title: Reporting coverage ranges from 10 entities in 1950 to 191 in 2004 and 2005.
insights.detail: The reporting count varies sharply in nearby years, including 62 in 2001, 190 in 2002, 55 in 2003, and 191 in 2004.
insights.caveat: A change in the yearly average can reflect changing coverage as well as changing observed rates.

insights.title: Only 8 entities report in every year from 1950 through 2005.
insights.detail: Their average across annual panel means is 10.67, versus 11.95 across all records.
insights.caveat: This fixed panel is a small, selected group and is not representative of the full world population.

insights.title: Year-over-year anomaly rules flag 122 changes by |z| > 2 and 235 by the 1.5×IQR rule.
insights.detail: There are 2,457 consecutive-year country changes; 122 are flagged by both methods.
insights.caveat: Flags identify unusual observed changes, not data errors or explanations; missing intervening years are not treated as annual changes.

insights.title: 82 observed rates exceed the distribution's Tukey IQR fences.
insights.detail: The maximum is 44.35 for Lithuania in 1996; no negative or zero rates occur.
insights.caveat: Extreme values are retained because a statistical outlier alone is not evidence of an invalid record.
